t.1.7.1: That heroic king had eight illustrious ministers, who were pure and devoted, ever engaged in the affairs of the kingdom.
t.1.7.2: Dhṛṣṭi, Jayanta, Vijaya, Siddhārtha, Arthasādhaka, Aśoka and Mantrapāla, and Sumantra was the eighth.
t.1.7.3: He had two esteemed officiating priests, the best of sages, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, and likewise other ministers as well.
t.1.7.4: They were illustrious and high-souled, learned in the śāstras and firm in valour, renowned and ever attentive, carrying out every command just as it was given.
t.1.7.5: Endowed with splendor, forbearance and renown, they spoke with a smile before addressing others; neither from anger nor for the sake of desire or gain would they ever speak an untrue word.
t.1.7.6: Nothing was unknown to them, whether in their own affairs or in those of others: what was being done, what had been done, and, through their spies, even what was intended.
t.1.7.7: Skilled in affairs of state and proven in friendship, they would administer punishment as the occasion required, even to their own sons.
t.1.7.8: They were diligent in gathering the treasury and in maintaining the army, and they would not harm even a hostile man if he had done no wrong.
t.1.7.10: Without harming brahmins or kṣatriyas, they filled the treasury; they were very stern in punishment, having carefully weighed each man's strength and weakness.
t.1.7.9: Of steadfast vigour and devoted to the science of kingship, they were ever the protectors of heroes and of the upright people dwelling in the realm.
t.1.7.11: Among all those ministers, pure, of one mind and fully discerning, there was nowhere, whether in the city or in the kingdom, a single man who spoke falsehood.
t.1.7.12: There was not a single wicked man there, nor any man who delighted in another's wife. The whole kingdom and that excellent city were entirely at peace.
t.1.7.13: They were all finely clothed and well adorned, men of excellent character, devoted to the welfare of the king, who kept watchful vigil with the eye of sound policy.
t.1.7.15: Furnished with such ministers as these, endowed with virtues, the sinless King Daśaratha ruled the earth.
t.1.7.14: They were held in esteem by their teacher for their virtues and renowned for their feats of valor; on account of the firmness of their judgment they were known everywhere, even in foreign lands.
t.1.7.16: Watching over his subjects through spies and delighting them with righteousness, he found no enemy who was either superior or equal to himself.
t.1.7.17: Surrounded by those ministers, devoted to sound counsel, steadfast, loyal, skilful and capable, that king, united with them, attained splendour, like the risen sun with its radiant rays.
